requirements.original: If the referenced module control function does not have any parameters, the parameter list may also be omitted at the place of invocation.
requirements.canonical: If the referenced module control function has no parameters, the parameter list MAY be omitted at the place of invocation.
requirements.condition: the referenced module control function does not have any parameters

ambiguity.issue: 'parameter list' at the invocation means the actual parameter list (the parentheses).

requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.3 -- If the referenced module control function does not have any parameters, the parameter list may also be omitted at the place of invocation.

requirements.original: Within every configuration there shall be one (and only one) Main Test Component (MTC).
requirements.canonical: A test configuration SHALL contain exactly one Main Test Component (MTC).
requirements.header: // @requirement: 9.0 -- Within every configuration there shall be one (and only one) Main Test Component (MTC).

requirements.original: The MTC shall be created by the system automatically at the start of each test case execution.
requirements.canonical: The MTC SHALL be created automatically by the test system at the start of each test case execution.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 9.0 -- The MTC shall be created by the system automatically at the start of each test case execution.

requirements.original: The behaviour defined in the body of the test case shall execute on this component.
requirements.canonical: The behaviour defined in the body of a test case SHALL execute on the MTC.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 9.0 -- The behaviour defined in the body of the test case shall execute on this component.

requirements.original: During execution of a test case, other components can be created dynamically by the explicit use of the create operation.
requirements.canonical: During test case execution, test components other than the MTC CAN be created dynamically by explicit use of the `create` operation.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 9.0 -- During execution of a test case, other components can be created dynamically by the explicit use of the create operation.

requirements.original: Test case execution shall end when the MTC terminates.
requirements.canonical: Test case execution SHALL end when the MTC terminates.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 9.0 -- Test case execution shall end when the MTC terminates.

requirements.original: All other PTCs are treated equally i.e. there is no explicit hierarchical relationship among them and the termination of a single PTC terminates neither other components nor the MTC.
requirements.canonical: The termination of a single PTC IS NOT terminating any other test component.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 9.0 -- All other PTCs are treated equally i.e. there is no explicit hierarchical relationship among them and the termination of a single PTC terminates neither other components nor the MTC.

requirements.original: All other PTCs are treated equally i.e. there is no explicit hierarchical relationship among them and the termination of a single PTC terminates neither other components nor the MTC.
requirements.canonical: The termination of a single PTC IS NOT terminating the MTC.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 9.0 -- All other PTCs are treated equally i.e. there is no explicit hierarchical relationship among them and the termination of a single PTC terminates neither other components nor the MTC.

requirements.original: When the MTC terminates, the test system has to stop all PTCs not terminated by the moment when the test case execution is ended.
requirements.canonical: When the MTC terminates, the test system SHALL stop all PTCs that are not yet terminated when the test case execution ends.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 9.0 -- When the MTC terminates, the test system has to stop all PTCs not terminated by the moment when the test case execution is ended.

requirements.original: Communication between test components and between the components and the test system interface is achieved via communication ports (see clause 9.1).
requirements.canonical: Communication between test components and between test components and the test system interface IS performed via communication ports.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 9.0 -- Communication between test components and between the components and the test system interface is achieved via communication ports (see clause 9.1).

requirements.original: Test component types and port types, denoted by the keywords component and port, shall be defined in the module definitions part.
requirements.canonical: A component type (keyword `component`) SHALL be defined in the module definitions part.

ambiguity.issue: 'Test component types' is used where the standard elsewhere says 'component type'.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 9.0 -- Test component types and port types, denoted by the keywords component and port, shall be defined in the module definitions part.

requirements.original: Test component types and port types, denoted by the keywords component and port, shall be defined in the module definitions part.
requirements.canonical: A port type (keyword `port`) SHALL be defined in the module definitions part.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 9.0 -- Test component types and port types, denoted by the keywords component and port, shall be defined in the module definitions part.

requirements.original: The actual configuration of components and the connections between them is achieved by performing create and connect operations within the test case behaviour.
requirements.canonical: The actual test configuration of test components and the connections between them IS established by performing `create` and `connect` operations within the test case behaviour.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 9.0 -- The actual configuration of components and the connections between them is achieved by performing create and connect operations within the test case behaviour.

requirements.original: The component ports are connected to the ports of the test system interface by means of the map operation (see clause 21.1.1).
requirements.canonical: A port of a test component IS connected to a port of the test system interface by means of the `map` operation.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 9.0 -- The component ports are connected to the ports of the test system interface by means of the map operation (see clause 21.1.1).

requirements.original: Test components are connected via their ports, i.e. connections among components and between a component and the test system interface are port-oriented.
requirements.canonical: A connection among test components and between a test component and the test system interface IS port-oriented, i.e. established between ports.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 9.1 -- Test components are connected via their ports, i.e. connections among components and between a component and the test system interface are port-oriented.

requirements.original: Each port is modelled as an infinite FIFO queue which stores the incoming messages or procedure calls until they are processed by the component owning that port (see figure 5).
requirements.canonical: A port IS modelled as an infinite FIFO queue.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 9.1 -- Each port is modelled as an infinite FIFO queue which stores the incoming messages or procedure calls until they are processed by the component owning that port (see figure 5).

requirements.original: Each port is modelled as an infinite FIFO queue which stores the incoming messages or procedure calls until they are processed by the component owning that port (see figure 5).
requirements.canonical: A port queue IS storing the incoming messages or procedure calls until they are processed by the test component owning that port.

ambiguity.issue: 'procedure calls' may be meant literally or as shorthand for all procedure-based communication (calls, replies, exceptions); the broader reading was chosen.
readings: A port queue IS storing incoming messages and all procedure-based items (calls, replies and exceptions) until they are processed by the owning test component.
A port queue IS storing only incoming messages and procedure calls until they are processed by the owning test component.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 9.1 -- Each port is modelled as an infinite FIFO queue which stores the incoming messages or procedure calls until they are processed by the component owning that port (see figure 5).

requirements.original: There are no restrictions on the number of connections a component may maintain.
requirements.canonical: A test component MAY maintain any number of connections.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 9.1 -- There are no restrictions on the number of connections a component may maintain.

requirements.original: One-to-many connections are also allowed (e.g. figure 6 (g) or (h)).
requirements.canonical: A one-to-many connection MAY be established.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 9.1 -- One-to-many connections are also allowed (e.g. figure 6 (g) or (h)).

requirements.original: A port owned by a component A shall not be connected with two or more ports owned by the same component (figure 7 (a) and (e)).
requirements.canonical: A port owned by a test component A SHALL NOT be connected with two or more ports owned by component A itself.

ambiguity.issue: 'the same component' can refer to component A itself or to any single component; since item 9.1-s015 separately covers ports of a different component B, the reading 'component A itself' was chosen.
readings: A port owned by a test component A SHALL NOT be connected with two or more ports owned by component A itself.
A port owned by a test component A SHALL NOT be connected with two or more ports owned by any single test component (A or another one).

requirements.header: // @requirement: 9.1 -- A port owned by a component A shall not be connected with two or more ports owned by the same component (figure 7 (a) and (e)).

requirements.original: A port of a test system interface cannot have connection with more than one port owned by a component A. This means, connections as shown in figure 7 (b) are not allowed.
requirements.canonical: A port of the test system interface SHALL NOT be connected with more than one port owned by the same test component.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 9.1 -- A port of a test system interface cannot have connection with more than one port owned by a component A. This means, connections as shown in figure 7 (b) are not allowed.

requirements.original: A port owned by a component A shall not be connected with two or more ports owned by a component B (see figure 7 (c)).
requirements.canonical: A port owned by a test component A SHALL NOT be connected with two or more ports owned by another test component B.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 9.1 -- A port owned by a component A shall not be connected with two or more ports owned by a component B (see figure 7 (c)).

requirements.original: A port owned by a component A can only have a one-to-one connection with the test system interface. This means, connections as shown in figure 7 (d) are not allowed.
requirements.canonical: A port owned by a test component SHALL have at most a one-to-one connection with the test system interface, i.e. it SHALL NOT be connected to more than one port of the test system interface.

ambiguity.issue: 'one-to-one' could restrict only the component port side or also the test system interface port side; since one-to-many connections are allowed (figure 6) and 9.1-s014 only restricts ports of the same component, the component-side reading was chosen.
readings: A port owned by a test component SHALL NOT be mapped to more than one port of the test system interface.
A port owned by a test component and the test system interface port it is mapped to SHALL both have no other mapping.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 9.1 -- A port owned by a component A can only have a one-to-one connection with the test system interface. This means, connections as shown in figure 7 (d) are not allowed.

requirements.original: Connections within the test system interface are not allowed (see figure 7 (f)).
requirements.canonical: A port of the test system interface SHALL NOT be connected with another port of the test system interface.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 9.1 -- Connections within the test system interface are not allowed (see figure 7 (f)).

requirements.original: A port that is connected shall not be mapped and a port that is mapped shall not be connected (see figure 7 (g)).
requirements.canonical: A port that is connected SHALL NOT be mapped.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 9.1 -- A port that is connected shall not be mapped and a port that is mapped shall not be connected (see figure 7 (g)).

requirements.original: A port that is connected shall not be mapped and a port that is mapped shall not be connected (see figure 7 (g)).
requirements.canonical: A port that is mapped SHALL NOT be connected.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 9.1 -- A port that is connected shall not be mapped and a port that is mapped shall not be connected (see figure 7 (g)).

requirements.original: The checks shall be made at runtime and shall lead to a test case error when failing.
requirements.canonical: A TTCN-3 tool SHALL check the restrictions on connections at runtime.

ambiguity.issue: It is unclear whether all connection checks or only those that cannot be performed at compile-time shall be made at runtime; the latter reading was chosen as most likely, but the canonical is phrased generally.
readings: A TTCN-3 tool SHALL check at runtime those connection restrictions that cannot be checked at compile-time.
A TTCN-3 tool SHALL check all connection restrictions at runtime, regardless of compile-time checks.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 9.1 -- The checks shall be made at runtime and shall lead to a test case error when failing.

requirements.original: The checks shall be made at runtime and shall lead to a test case error when failing.
requirements.canonical: A failing runtime check of a connection restriction SHALL lead to a test case error.
requirements.condition: a runtime connection restriction check fails
requirements.header: // @requirement: 9.1 -- The checks shall be made at runtime and shall lead to a test case error when failing.

requirements.original: Instead, a well defined (but abstract) test system interface shall be associated with each test case.
requirements.canonical: A well-defined abstract test system interface SHALL be associated with each test case.

ambiguity.issue: This conflicts on its face with 9.2-s023 (test system interface need not be associated when only the MTC is used); the reading that the association may be implicit was chosen.
readings: Each test case SHALL have a test system interface, either explicitly given (system clause) or implicitly defined by the MTC component type.
Each test case SHALL explicitly declare a test system interface.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 9.2 -- Instead, a well defined (but abstract) test system interface shall be associated with each test case.

requirements.original: The test system interface statically defines the number and type of the port connections to the SUT during a test run.
requirements.canonical: The test system interface IS statically defining the number and type of the port connections to the SUT during a test run.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 9.2 -- The test system interface statically defines the number and type of the port connections to the SUT during a test run.

requirements.original: However, the connections between the test system interface and the TTCN-3 test components are dynamic in nature and may be modified during a test run by using map and unmap operations (see clause 21.1).
requirements.canonical: A connection between the test system interface and a test component MAY be modified during a test run by using `map` and `unmap` operations.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 9.2 -- However, the connections between the test system interface and the TTCN-3 test components are dynamic in nature and may be modified during a test run by using map and unmap operations (see clause 21.1).

requirements.original: Generally, a component type reference defining the test system interface shall be associated with every test case using more than one test component.
requirements.canonical: A test case using more than one test component SHALL be associated with a component type reference defining the test system interface.
requirements.condition: the test case uses more than one test component

ambiguity.issue: 'Generally' weakens the SHALL; it is unclear whether it is a strict rule or a general guideline with exceptions.
readings: A test case using more than one test component SHALL have a `system` clause referencing a component type.
A test case using more than one test component SHOULD normally have a `system` clause; omitting it is not an error.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 9.2 -- Generally, a component type reference defining the test system interface shall be associated with every test case using more than one test component.

requirements.original: The ports of the test system interface shall automatically be instantiated by the system together with the MTC when the test case execution starts.
requirements.canonical: The ports of the test system interface SHALL be instantiated automatically by the test system together with the MTC when the test case execution starts.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 9.2 -- The ports of the test system interface shall automatically be instantiated by the system together with the MTC when the test case execution starts.

requirements.original: The operation returning the component reference of the test system interface is system.
requirements.canonical: The `system` operation IS returning the component reference of the test system interface.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 9.2 -- The operation returning the component reference of the test system interface is system.

requirements.original: This shall be used to address the ports of the test system.
requirements.canonical: The `system` operation SHALL be used to address the ports of the test system interface.

ambiguity.issue: 'ports of the test system' is used where 'ports of the test system interface' is meant.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 9.2 -- This shall be used to address the ports of the test system.

requirements.original: In the case where the MTC is the only component that is instantiated during test execution, a test system interface need not be associated to the test case.
requirements.canonical: When the MTC is the only test component instantiated during test execution, a test system interface NEED NOT be associated to the test case.
requirements.condition: the MTC is the only test component instantiated during test execution
requirements.header: // @requirement: 9.2 -- In the case where the MTC is the only component that is instantiated during test execution, a test system interface need not be associated to the test case.

requirements.original: In this case, the component type definition associated with the MTC implicitly defines the corresponding test system interface.
requirements.canonical: When the MTC is the only test component instantiated during test execution, the component type associated with the MTC IS implicitly defining the test system interface.
requirements.condition: the MTC is the only test component and no test system interface is associated
requirements.header: // @requirement: 9.2 -- In this case, the component type definition associated with the MTC implicitly defines the corresponding test system interface.

requirements.original: a) The same as for component type definitions (see clause 6.2.10.1).
requirements.canonical: A test system interface definition SHALL satisfy the same restrictions as a component type definition.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 9.2 -- a) The same as for component type definitions (see clause 6.2.10.1).

requirements.original: After value assignment, they do not change their value during test execution.
requirements.canonical: After value assignment, a constant SHALL NOT change its value during test execution.
requirements.condition: the constant has been assigned its value
requirements.header: // @requirement: 10 -- After value assignment, they do not change their value during test execution.

requirements.original: They can be used on the right hand side of assignments, in expressions, in actual parameters, and in template definitions.
requirements.canonical: A constant MAY be used on the right hand side of an assignment, in an expression, in an actual parameter and in a template definition.

examples.text:
const integer c_myConst1 := 1;
  const boolean c_myConst2 := true, c_myConst3 := false;

requirements.header: // @requirement: 10 -- They can be used on the right hand side of assignments, in expressions, in actual parameters, and in template definitions.

requirements.original: Constants used within type definitions have to have values known at compile-time.
requirements.canonical: A constant used within a type definition SHALL have a value known at compile-time.
requirements.condition: the constant is used within a type definition
requirements.header: // @requirement: 10 -- Constants used within type definitions have to have values known at compile-time.

requirements.original: const [ TypeOrNestedTypeDef ] { ConstIdentifier [ ArrayDef ] ":=" ConstantExpression [ "," ] } [ ";" ]
requirements.canonical: A constant declaration has the syntax `const` [TypeOrNestedTypeDef] followed by one or more ConstIdentifier [ArrayDef] ":=" ConstantExpression items optionally separated by ",", optionally terminated by ";".

examples.text:
const integer c_myConst1 := 1;
  const boolean c_myConst2 := true, c_myConst3 := false;

requirements.header: // @requirement: 10 -- const [ TypeOrNestedTypeDef ] { ConstIdentifier [ ArrayDef ] ":=" ConstantExpression [ "," ] } [ ";" ]

requirements.original: A value is assigned only once to a constant, at the place of its declaration.
requirements.canonical: A value SHALL be assigned to a constant only once, at the place of the constant declaration.

examples.text:
const integer c_myConst1 := 1;
  const boolean c_myConst2 := true, c_myConst3 := false;

requirements.header: // @requirement: 10 -- A value is assigned only once to a constant, at the place of its declaration.

requirements.original: The constant does not change its value during test execution.
requirements.canonical: A constant SHALL NOT change its value during test execution.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 10 -- The constant does not change its value during test execution.

requirements.original: The constant is defined only once, but can be referenced multiple times in a TTCN-3 module.
requirements.canonical: A constant SHALL be defined only once in a TTCN-3 module.

readings: A constant identifier SHALL be declared only once within its scope.
Each constant SHALL have exactly one definition (no separate declaration and definition) in a TTCN-3 module.
ambiguity.issue: "defined only once" can be read as a uniqueness-of-identifier rule or as describing single definition; the first (uniqueness within scope, cf. clause 5) is chosen as the testable reading.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 10 -- The constant is defined only once, but can be referenced multiple times in a TTCN-3 module.

requirements.original: The constant is defined only once, but can be referenced multiple times in a TTCN-3 module.
requirements.canonical: A constant MAY be referenced multiple times in a TTCN-3 module.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 10 -- The constant is defined only once, but can be referenced multiple times in a TTCN-3 module.

requirements.original: The type of the constant is either provided explicitly or implicitly according to the rules for automatic typing specified in the clause 6.5.
requirements.canonical: The type of a constant IS either provided explicitly or determined implicitly according to the rules for automatic typing.

examples.text:
const integer c_myConst1 := 1;
  const boolean c_myConst2 := true, c_myConst3 := false;

requirements.header: // @requirement: 10 -- The type of the constant is either provided explicitly or implicitly according to the rules for automatic typing specified in the clause 6.5.

requirements.original: When automatic typing is used, the TypeOrNestedParDef part is missing and the type is equal to the type of the expression on the right-hand side of the assignment.
requirements.canonical: When automatic typing is used, the TypeOrNestedTypeDef part of the constant declaration IS missing.

ambiguity.issue: The syntax block uses TypeOrNestedTypeDef; TypeOrNestedParDef is not part of the constant declaration syntax.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 10 -- When automatic typing is used, the TypeOrNestedParDef part is missing and the type is equal to the type of the expression on the right-hand side of the assignment.

requirements.original: When automatic typing is used, the TypeOrNestedParDef part is missing and the type is equal to the type of the expression on the right-hand side of the assignment.
requirements.canonical: When automatic typing is used, the type of a constant IS equal to the type of the expression on the right hand side of the assignment.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 10 -- When automatic typing is used, the TypeOrNestedParDef part is missing and the type is equal to the type of the expression on the right-hand side of the assignment.

requirements.original: Optional fields of record and set constants or constant fields can be initialized explicitly or implicitly.
requirements.canonical: An optional field of a record or set constant or of a constant field MAY be initialized explicitly or implicitly.

readings: An optional field of a record or set constant, or an optional field of a record or set field of a constant, MAY be initialized explicitly or implicitly.
An optional field of a record or set constant, or an optional field of a field of a constant of any structured type, MAY be initialized explicitly or implicitly.
ambiguity.issue: "constant fields" is not defined; read as fields (of record/set type) nested inside a constant. The first reading is chosen.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 10 -- Optional fields of record and set constants or constant fields can be initialized explicitly or implicitly.

requirements.original: For implicit initialization of the optional fields of a constant or a constant field, an optional attribute with the value "implicit omit" (see clause 27.7) shall be associated with it either directly or via the attribute distribution (scoping) mechanism (see clause 27.1.1).
requirements.canonical: For implicit initialization of the optional fields of a constant or a constant field, an optional attribute with the value "implicit omit" SHALL be associated with the constant or constant field either directly or via the attribute distribution (scoping) mechanism.
requirements.condition: the optional fields of a constant or constant field are to be initialized implicitly
requirements.header: // @requirement: 10 -- For implicit initialization of the optional fields of a constant or a constant field, an optional attribute with the value "implicit omit" (see clause 27.7) shall be associated with it either directly or via the attribute distribution (scoping) mechanism (see clause 27.1.1).

requirements.original: b) Constant expressions initializing constants, which are used in type and array definitions, shall only contain literals, predefined functions except of rnd (see clause 16.1.2), operators specified in clause 7.1, and other constants obeying the limitations of this clause.
requirements.canonical: A constant expression initializing a constant that is used in a type or array definition SHALL only contain literals, predefined functions except `rnd`, operators specified in clause 7.1, and other constants obeying the limitations of clause 10.
requirements.condition: the constant is used in a type definition or array definition
requirements.header: // @requirement: 10 -- b) Constant expressions initializing constants, which are used in type and array definitions, shall only contain literals, predefined functions except of rnd (see clause 16.1.2), operators specified in clause 7.1, and other constants obeying the limitations of this clause.

requirements.original: b) Constant expressions initializing constants, which are used in type and array definitions, shall only contain literals, predefined functions except of rnd (see clause 16.1.2), operators specified in clause 7.1, and other constants obeying the limitations of this clause.
requirements.canonical: A constant expression initializing a constant that is used in a type or array definition SHALL NOT contain a call of the predefined function `rnd`.
requirements.condition: the constant is used in a type definition or array definition
requirements.header: // @requirement: 10 -- b) Constant expressions initializing constants, which are used in type and array definitions, shall only contain literals, predefined functions except of rnd (see clause 16.1.2), operators specified in clause 7.1, and other constants obeying the limitations of this clause.

requirements.original: NOTE: The only value that can be assigned to global constants of default, component, port or timer type or component constants of default or component types is the special value null.
requirements.canonical: The only value that can be assigned to a global constant of default, component, port or timer type, or to a component constant of default or component type, IS the special value `null`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 10 -- NOTE: The only value that can be assigned to global constants of default, component, port or timer type or component constants of default or component types is the special value null.

requirements.original: c) Using the dot notation (see clauses 6.2.1.1, 6.2.2.1 and 6.2.5.1) and index notation (see clauses 6.2.7 and 6.2.3.0) for referencing a field, alternative or element of an address value, which actual value is null shall cause an error.
requirements.canonical: Referencing a field, alternative or element of an address value whose actual value is `null` using dot notation or index notation SHALL cause an error.

readings: Referencing a field, alternative or element of a constant of address type whose actual value is `null` using dot or index notation SHALL cause an error.
Referencing a field, alternative or element of any address value (constant, variable or parameter) whose actual value is `null` using dot or index notation SHALL cause an error.
ambiguity.issue: The restriction is located in the constants clause but is not limited to constants in its wording; also unclear whether the error is a compile-time or runtime error. The general reading (any address value) is used in canonical.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 10 -- c) Using the dot notation (see clauses 6.2.1.1, 6.2.2.1 and 6.2.5.1) and index notation (see clauses 6.2.7 and 6.2.3.0) for referencing a field, alternative or element of an address value, which actual value is null shall cause an error.

requirements.original: d) The right-hand side of the assignment that initializes a constant shall evaluate to an object that is at least partially initialized.
requirements.canonical: The right hand side of the assignment that initializes a constant SHALL evaluate to an object that is at least partially initialized.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 10 -- d) The right-hand side of the assignment that initializes a constant shall evaluate to an object that is at least partially initialized.

requirements.original: e) _ConstantExpression shall evaluate to a value which is type compatible with TypeOrNestedTypeDef._ f) If the TypeOrNestedTypeDef part is missing from the declaration, the ArrayDef part shall be missing as well and the assignment part (i.e. ":=" ConstantExpression) shall be present.
requirements.canonical: The ConstantExpression of a constant declaration SHALL evaluate to a value that is type compatible with the TypeOrNestedTypeDef.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 10 -- e) _ConstantExpression shall evaluate to a value which is type compatible with TypeOrNestedTypeDef._ f) If the TypeOrNestedTypeDef part is missing from the declaration, the ArrayDef part shall be missing as well and the assignment part (i.e. ":=" ConstantExpression) shall be present.

requirements.original: e) _ConstantExpression shall evaluate to a value which is type compatible with TypeOrNestedTypeDef._ f) If the TypeOrNestedTypeDef part is missing from the declaration, the ArrayDef part shall be missing as well and the assignment part (i.e. ":=" ConstantExpression) shall be present.
requirements.canonical: If the TypeOrNestedTypeDef part is missing from a constant declaration, the ArrayDef part SHALL be missing as well.
requirements.condition: the TypeOrNestedTypeDef part is missing from the declaration
requirements.header: // @requirement: 10 -- e) _ConstantExpression shall evaluate to a value which is type compatible with TypeOrNestedTypeDef._ f) If the TypeOrNestedTypeDef part is missing from the declaration, the ArrayDef part shall be missing as well and the assignment part (i.e. ":=" ConstantExpression) shall be present.

requirements.original: e) _ConstantExpression shall evaluate to a value which is type compatible with TypeOrNestedTypeDef._ f) If the TypeOrNestedTypeDef part is missing from the declaration, the ArrayDef part shall be missing as well and the assignment part (i.e. ":=" ConstantExpression) shall be present.
requirements.canonical: If the TypeOrNestedTypeDef part is missing from a constant declaration, the assignment part (":=" ConstantExpression) SHALL be present.
requirements.condition: the TypeOrNestedTypeDef part is missing from the declaration
requirements.header: // @requirement: 10 -- e) _ConstantExpression shall evaluate to a value which is type compatible with TypeOrNestedTypeDef._ f) If the TypeOrNestedTypeDef part is missing from the declaration, the ArrayDef part shall be missing as well and the assignment part (i.e. ":=" ConstantExpression) shall be present.
